fix/bestiary-globals — the classic-script -> ES-module globals bridge. data/bestiary.js, data/realm-bestiary.js, data/monster-flavor.js, and data/model-recipes.js each declare their payload as a top-level `const` (BESTIARY/REALM_BESTIARY/MONSTER_FLAVOR/MODEL_RECIPES). Classic <script> tags share one declarative scope, so other classic scripts see those consts as bare identifiers already (e.g. src/engine/theater-data.js reads PART_NAMES directly) — but top-level const/let, unlike var/function declarations, never attaches to `window`. An ES module (src/ui/ref-bestiary.js) has its own module scope and can only reach classic-script data through `window`, so before this fix window.BESTIARY etc. were always undefined and the Monster Manual's manualEntries() silently fell back to {} — empty grid, dead filters. This file runs after all four data consts (and after data/model-recipe-overrides.js) and republishes each one onto window explicitly (typeof-guarded, never redeclares them — owns nothing new, a pure republish) so any current or future ES-module Reference Shelf app has one shared, explicit seam instead of each module re-deriving its own defensive copy. Must load before any `<script type="module">` tag that reads these off window (today: src/ui/ref-bestiary.js). Added 2026-07-06 (fix/bestiary-globals).

The Sundering flag (w.sundered) is set from the existing clock_fired handler in world.dm when the Doom front's clock fires before it closes — the dark twin ending, uncrownable forever; the full legend testament is C2's job. Zero new model calls — every check here is a synchronous read; the ritual (C2) is the only place dice are cast.

CROWNING §7.C2 (docs/CROWNING-BASTION.md): the ritual + legend state. The player-initiated Crowning ceremony — a bardo-pattern modal (reuses #bardoModal/#bardoBody, openBardo's mold) with three click-rolls (Legend via CROWN_LEGEND, Crown epithet via the existing epithet_grant round-trip, Succession over the computed testament) + a computed testament (computeSaga). crownWorld() writes the additive w.crowned state (the non-destructive answer to destroyWorld, which never banked souls), retires the crowned PC to U.souls via crownRetireToSoul (Q2 — c.status becomes a NEW 'crowned' value, retired in place, not deleted), and feeds legendRecord's U.legends universe pool (capped at U_LEGENDS_CAP, oldest evicted) — which src/world/gap-wiring.js's distantWordPick widens Distant Word with (§3.4, cross-region gossip with a mechanical source). markSundered(w) is the Sundering's (C1's w.sundered flag) shared legend pass, inverted valence, idempotent, called from C1's clock_fired block in world.dm via a typeof guard. Zero new model calls — every roll is a deterministic click-roll; the DM's crowning narration rides the turn it would have narrated anyway.

Persistence + the World Spine: localStorage universe (loadU/saveU), in-world clock, the World State Ledger (append-only), the node-graph map, and additive legacy-save migration. The live mutable global U stays app-owned (transient state like SEED/ORC lives in GS); these read/write U at call-time.

The relational entity store (docs/CODEX.md): NPC/Location/Item/Faction records with rolled (verbatim) + fields (player-safe) + dm (DM-only) + typed links[] (wikilinks) + status{known,soft,at,condition}. Two-tier lifecycle: SOFT entities are a recontextualizable pool (codexRecontextualize preserves the rolled soul, reassigns context); the player TOUCHING one locks it to canon forever (codexContact; recontextualize refuses on hard records). codexDigest = all-seeing DM slice; codexPlayerView = knowledge-gated sanitized projection. Written only via codex_* events in world.dm; ensureCodex migrates gazetteer/factions in (idempotent, non-destructive). Phase 1 of CODEX.md. MODEL-GRAMMAR G2 §4b: codexResolveShapeOnMint resolves a DM-authored `rec.shape` hint through src/engine/theater-data.js's pure resolveShapeHint at MINT time only (codexAdd's new-record path + codexUpdate's shape-not-yet-set path) — canon-locks the result onto `r.shape` (additive field) and writes one `drift`/`shape-gap` ledger line per dropped/unknown part name via addLedger (the growth signal). Once `r.shape` is set, both codexAdd's merge path and codexUpdate refuse to overwrite it (the mogwai clause: 'looks like YOUR mogwai forever').

REPUTATION (docs/REPUTATION.md): the world remembers what it SAW. w.renown = {factions:{slug:{score,epithets}}, regions:{regionId:{score,epithets}}} — pure ledger math, zero DM invention (the twin of world.turn's recall). repuApplyDeed prices a witnessed-or-claimed deed (repuWitnessed's script-default inference: co-located codex witnesses OR an inhabited node OR a fled foe survivor; payload.witnessed overrides), attributes to the deed's faction + rivals (half weight, opposite sign — no structured rival-pair map exists yet, so every other faction proxies as a rival) + the node's region; mints a PERMANENT epithet request (dm.needsEpithet, mirroring dm.needsEffectDie) at 2x a level-appropriate E(L) (engine.advancement's encounterUnit). repuFadeTick (called from world.turn's montage) decays scores toward 0 (RENOWN_FADE/month, snap under RENOWN_ZERO); epithets never fade. Consumers: repuOpeningAttitudeShift (caps +-2, feeds codexGetAttitude's lazy init), repuHunted/repuHuntedBy (score <= HUNTED_AT biases WORLD-TURN pressure bearings), repuStandingWord (the coarse hated/wary/neutral/known/honored player-facing word — never the raw score).

The Saga: a character's most significant entities (NPCs/enemies/factions/places/threads), derived + ranked from the world ledger + gazetteer + faction web by stake × frequency × recency. computeSaga(w,c) reads; refreshSaga(w,c) persists onto c.saga. The dead PC's Saga is what the 14 bardo vision-rolls act on (docs/DEATH-AND-REBIRTH.md, build step 1). Added 2026-06-21.

The death→rebirth loop (docs/DEATH-AND-REBIRTH.md). Step 2: the bardo gap — rollBardoGap() is a 0–49 in-world-day bell roll (triangular, mode ~3–4 weeks); bardoGap(w,[days]) advances the world clock by the gap and turns the faction web once per elapsed week. Step 3: the 14 vision-rolls — bardoVisions(w,c) dreams 7 peaceful + 7 wrathful outcomes over the dead PC's Saga (fireVision mutates faction clocks / NPC + place fate / threads via applyVision, writes the truth to the ledger, surfaces a Fragment to the player; VISION_OUTCOMES is draft flavor pending an authored table). runBardo(w,c) orchestrates refreshSaga→gap→visions, storing c.visions. Step 5: corpse + loot decay — a fallen PC's body+effects persist (set at death); corpseStatus(w,c) decays fresh→disturbed→gone by elapsed in-world days vs the body's CORPSE_CONTEXTS; corpsesAt(w,node) finds recoverable bodies; claimCorpse(w,c,taker) transfers the haul. Layer 2 (query/logic; only L1/L2 deps). Added 2026-06-21.

The item lifecycle contract (docs/ITEM-LEGACY.md) — death → corpse → scavenge → recovery custody, tracked on the CODEX item record under one block r.legacy (the seven GPT lifecycle fields: origin/claimant/lastSeen/lossState/recoveryHook/factionInterest/decay-pointer + an instSnapshot re-mint truth). The inventory instance gains ZERO new fields; the existing inst.codexId link is the only seam. legacyGrade(inst) is the significance gate (codex-storied OR enchanted non-consumable non-stack). legacyEnsureRecord mints/ensures the record + r.legacy (auto-promotes an enchanted item at death); legacyStamp is the sole r.legacy writer after ensure (touches the record for the delta digest + one ledger line). corpseLegacyStamp (from killCharacter, world.fate) stamps every legacy-grade carried item on-corpse + mints a recovery-hook thread (legacyMintHook, reusing the thread-seed pattern). corpseScavengeResolve is the enemy-gets-your-gear path — a LAZY, once-per-corpse engine d6 (SCAVENGE_TEETH: den 3 / travelled 2 / wild 1 / sealed 0) fired only at claimCorpse + runBardo (never on a read path); a hit moves one item to claimed-creature/npc/faction, a gone corpse sweeps the rest to unknown. legacyDigest is the dmDigest itemLegacy slice (null when empty, cap 5). One new event item_claimed + item_changed takenBy widening carry the custody moves. INFERENCE COST ZERO — no model call anywhere. lossState:"cached" is the parked-Bastion seam (refused in v1). Layer 2. Added 2026-07-06 (ITEM-LEGACY unit).

REFERENCE-SHELF.md unit S1 — the opening-screen reference-app launcher framework. REFERENCE_APPS is a module-owned registry ({id,label,icon,order,mount(container),teardown(container)}); referenceShelfRegister(entry) pushes + sorts by order. referenceShelfSectionHTML() renders a labeled Reference section (one button per registered app) that renderStart() appends after the Begin-button block (guarded typeof!=="undefined" for jsdom). referenceShelfOpen(id)/referenceShelfClose() own the shared #refShelf overlay's lifecycle — exactly one app mounted at a time (switching/closing calls the outgoing app's teardown first), Esc-close, and a Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap. THE REGISTRATION-TIMING LAW: ES-module reference apps (Monster Manual, Wiki) register AFTER the inline showTab('start') boot call, so the first renderStart() paint predates them — referenceShelfRegister therefore re-invokes renderStart() whenever #panel-start is the active panel, so late registrants appear without a tab switch. Loaded before src/world/render.js in loadOrder. Added 2026-07-05.

BESTIARY-MANUAL.md unit S2 — the Monster Manual, REFERENCE-SHELF.md's registered app #1. A FIFTH ES-module boundary file (parallel to theater-boot/theater-verbs/theater-parts/theater-figures), own <script type="module"> tag in genesis.html loaded AFTER theater-boot.js's tag (so window.Theater.refFigure exists at this module's top-level registration time). Imports "three" via the shared importmap + resolveWholeObject from ./theater-figures.js; reads the classic-script globals BESTIARY/REALM_BESTIARY/MONSTER_FLAVOR/MODEL_RECIPES/theaterArchetypeFor/cmParseActionText off window (never declares them itself — the classic/module boundary stays one-way). manualEntries() is the pure data adapter yielding a uniform 1817-entry array (510 BESTIARY regular + 1307 REALM_BESTIARY realm; realm ids are DERIVED as realm+':'+slugify(name) with a -2/-3… collision suffix, since REALM_BESTIARY entries carry no id field; realm entries resolve ac/hp/speed/abilities/actions off BESTIARY[entry.frame], their own cr/type/size/traits/flavorTable/desc); exposed as window.manualEntries for the verification harness. The grid is a lazy IntersectonObserver mount/dispose over ONE shared offscreen WebGLRenderer that blits (drawImage, imageSmoothingEnabled=false) to each card's own 2D canvas (Fable's ruling: side-steps the ~16-context browser limit, makes the live-canvas cap (24) a soft number, static cards cost zero GL work after first paint — hover/focus triggers the only re-render). The detail view gets its own dedicated second WebGLRenderer/scene/camera (2 GL contexts total, constant) and always orbits; ships the alt-model bullet-menu MECHANISM (renders only when a resolved registry entry — or a test-injected stub via __setStubAlts — declares alts:[{label,module,fn}]; no real entry does today, so it's hidden everywhere in production). Every figure is built/disposed exclusively via window.Theater.refFigure (theater-boot.js's tiny additive seam next to window.Theater={...}) — this module never calls figureFor/clearGroup directly (both module-private) nor window.Theater.retire(). Filters (corpus/tier/type/size/CR range/has-flavor/has-desc/free-text name) persist to the URL query (mm_ prefixed params) so a filtered view is shareable/reproducible. Read-only in v1 (no write-back to data/*). `type:"module"` is EXEMPT in check-manifest.py from the classic loadOrder <script>-tag pairing check, same as the other theater-* ES-module files. Added 2026-07-05 (REFERENCE-SHELF wave 3, unit S2). Dashboard extension (BESTIARY-DASHBOARD.md, spec-locked 2026-07-06): a coverage header strip (whole-roster model-tier + QA-gap counts, toggleable chips), QA-gap filters (needs-desc/needs-flavor/frame-missing/frame-CR-drift tri-state selects), a per-creature edit-target copy bundle (editTargetFor, routing every edit surface to its SOURCE file, never the generated artifact), and a loud realm chassis-vs-skin provenance callout — all read-only, zero model calls.

The world-facing renders (DOM): the world panel, the hex map SVG, the route map, the ledger, the opening, powers, the start screen, and the universe shelf. Creator renders (renderBardo/renderCharge) live with the creator domain. shopPanel (docs/SHOP-UI.md §3) renders the tabbed Buy|Sell merchant panel — reads shopOf/shopAttitude (world.shop) + itemPrice/isConsumable/sellValue (engine.economy) for display only; every transaction routes through world.shop's buyItem/sellItem. combatPanel (docs/COMBAT-TRACKER.md) renders the read-only band-lane fight tracker over GS.combat — foe HP/AC never enter the DOM, only a derived state word (cmFoeStateWord); actionsAbilitiesBody now also fills from CLASS_PROGRESSION + ORIGIN_FEATS (§3). charSheetBody also surfaces REPUTATION.md §3's player surface: claimed epithets + a coarse standing word per revealed faction (repuEpithetsOf/repuStandingWord) — never the raw score. cmTheaterNotify(kind,data) (BATTLE-THEATER T3, §4, added 2026-07-03): the null-safe bridge from a classic-script ledger site to window.Theater.play — called from ≤8 sites in src/world/dm.js (attack/foe_action ×2/move_zone/foe_morale/crit_outcome/hp_changed's damage path), forwards through window.Theater.fxFromLedger (re-exported from the sealed ES-module src/ui/theater-verbs.js, since this file can't `import` it) to resolve a verb, then window.Theater.play(verb,opts); a no-op (never a throw) when window.Theater is absent — the standard headless/jsdom/no-WebGL degrade every Theater consumer already honors. renderArchiveVault/archiveVaultToggle (FOREVER-STORAGE.md §2 "viewable on demand from the Chronicle") is the Chronicle's archived-narration expander — a closed-by-default <details> that fetches archiveReadForWorld (world.store) into GS.archive only when opened and paints the cooled dmlog prose oldest-first; the archive read never sits on the render hot path.

Track-B compiled-tables dice engine: CT (reads window.GENESIS_TABLES from tables.js), rollExpr (flat/bell/mixed dice strings), rollTable (roll a compiled table by id). Distinct from engine.tables, which rolls the inline-data tables.

Segment walk-roller (docs/SESSION-PREP.md §2). rollUrbanWalk(opts) picks a topology (16 graph-shape pacing grammars), builds the segment graph, rolls each node's segment sub-table (dedup+overflow), encounter, and scene frame from the compiled tables (row[5] cells), and returns the walk as a data structure (segments=nodes, transitions=edges). Ported from the Obsidian 'Urban Procedure v3.1' Templater; no file/canvas output. WALK-REFRESH §2.1: also carries a per-segment loot lane (reuses dwalkBudget/dwalkAssignLoot/dwalkLoot from engine.dungeon-walk verbatim, called at runtime after full load-order — declared in a module that loads AFTER this one, same hoisting pattern the rest of the walk family already relies on; only the presentation frame — stash/lockbox/strongbox — differs). WALK-REFRESH §2.3: walkSpiceBand/walkIsStrangePlus gate a spice-graded chance that a Discovery segment/finale IS a rollItem macguffin. WALK-REFRESH §3: rollWalkSkin(envKind) rolls the compiled walk-skin-<envKind> table (null-safe until tables-wave1 authors it) — called by all three walk-rollers + travel walks (via rollWildernessWalk) at assembly, stored as walk.skin={text,band,ref}. WIRING-SWEEP-A §7 (docs/WIRING-MAP.md item 9, world.wiring-a): each non-finale segment additionally carries `interactable` via walkPickInteractable("urban") — urban-interactable-object, the same slot dungeon-walk.js already wires; null-safe (wiring-a.js absent/table uncompiled -> null, byte-identical to before).

WALK-REFRESH §1 — live rosters for the walk-rollers. A code-side registry (WALK_ARCHETYPES, keyed by the archetype string as it appears in the tables — wilderness enemy-category names + dungeon/urban threat-identity ids) mapping each to bestiary tag filters (type/sizeMax/habitatPref) + a per-tier/slot CR band. resolveArchetypePool(archetypeName,{tier,biome,slot},authoredPoolStr) unions the registry-filtered BESTIARY pool with the authored 'A / B / C' pool (the floor, kept present at ~35% weight — WALK_ARCHETYPE_FLOOR_WEIGHT) and returns one creature name string, byte-compatible with the old walkPickFromPool(pool) call sites. Unknown archetype or an empty bestiary match falls back to the authored pool only (graceful, today's exact behavior). Adam's 95 custom creatures enter rotation automatically (indexed with CR in data/bestiary.js) — a deliberate feature, not a side effect.

Dungeon walk-roller (docs/SESSION-PREP.md §2). rollDungeonWalk(opts): 12 topologies, depth-budgeted loot, affinity-filtered boss/revelation (by rolled Myth Seed) → dungeon data structure (rooms=nodes, doors=edges). Ported from the Obsidian 'Dungeon Procedure v4.2'. Reuses engine.walk generics. WALK-REFRESH: dwalkOutlandish/dwalkOutlandishAllowed (§2.2, PROVISIONAL null-safe level-gate on the future dungeon-loot-outlandish Band column) + a Strange+ plot-item chance on Discovery rooms (§2.3) + the rolled walk.skin (§3, via rollWalkSkin).

Wilderness leg-walk roller (docs/SESSION-PREP.md §2). rollWildernessWalk(opts): a linear journey of travel legs (biome can shift) + an arrival, each leg an encounter + travel texture → journey data structure (legs=nodes, route=edges). Authored from the wilderness table set (no source generator). Reuses engine.walk generics. WALK-REFRESH §2.1: also carries a per-leg loot lane (wwalkLootLane/wwalkLootFor reuse dwalkBudget/dwalkAssignLoot/dwalkLoot from engine.dungeon-walk verbatim; only the presentation frame — cache/remains/grave-goods — differs). WALK-REFRESH §2.3: a Strange+ plot-item chance on Discovery legs. WALK-REFRESH §3: the rolled walk.skin (null-safe until tables-wave1 lands) — also covers travel walks, since world.play's travel() calls this same roller. WIRING-SWEEP-A §7/§5 (docs/WIRING-MAP.md items 9+10, world.wiring-a): each leg additionally carries `interactable` (wilderness-interactable-object, same slot dungeon-walk.js wires) + `regionEncounter` (region-encounter, an additive regional-flavor roll gated on `region` being present — null region -> null, byte-identical fallback); both null-safe.

Quest-hook roller (docs/SYNTHESIS-CONTRACT.md). rollQuestHook({environment}) → raw hook material (destination flavor, macguffin, complication, urgency clock, questgiver-avoidance, pitch) bound to a prepped environment; questgiver identity left for the synthesis pass to assign. Reuses engine.walk's walkPick.

Prep-bundle assembler (docs/SYNTHESIS-CONTRACT.md) — the deterministic pre-step of the synthesis pass. assemblePrepBundle({world,tier,environments}) fires the multi-environment walk rollers, binds a quest hook to each, and gathers ledger context from the live world → the input bundle the staged synthesis prompts consume. prepBundleSummary() → the cheap Stage-1 view. TIYL-DEEPENING §3.4: pbundleTiylThread/pbundleApplyTiylBias bias the FIRST session's first environment's hook toward an unresolved TIYL thread when one exists (additive hook.tiylBias field only). No LLM.

The CODEX rollers (Phases 2+5; docs/CODEX.md §2) — the engine mints the atoms. rollNPC()/rollPlace()/rollItem()/rollBuildingInterior()/rollLoot() chain the compiled npc-*/place-*/plot-item/plot-lock/building-interior/dungeon-loot-* tables (via rollTable / the dungeon-walk budget chain) into a codexAdd-ready payload: `rolled` (raw dice verbatim), a player-safe `fields` glance-read, and DM-only `dm` levers; items carry a `source` pointer (§8b). They do NOT write the world — prep/the DM emit codex_add events. The AI assigns final meaning + wires links. BATCH3-PLAN unit 8 (docs/BREACH.md §2d): rollNPC also carries a rare breach-touched rider — NPC_BREACH_TOUCH (hand-authored PROVISIONAL d12 vocabulary) + touchedNpcChance/rollNpcBreachTouch (fray-scaled ~2%→8% via engine.region's frayLevel, optional/null-safe dep) — landing on `dm.breachTouch` only on the rare roll that clears the threshold; every other payload is byte-identical to before.

Skin grants + motif pervasion (docs/SKIN-GRANTS.md, BATCH3-GUARDRAILS J1/J2/J3) — the batch-3 unit that pays a skin's implied mechanical promise through rolled machinery instead of leaving it for the DM to freehand. applySkinGrants(walk, skin, w) runs AFTER base walk assembly (called from rollDungeonWalk/rollUrbanWalk/rollWildernessWalk once each has built its full segment/edge structure): it threads the motif kit (entrance beat on segment 1, a composed per-segment tint, threatBias feed + reskinVerb, hazard/footing tint, palette) via skinApplyMotif, then dispatches each comma-separated grant token (hoard/captive/faction-mark/threat-bias:<tag>/hazard-suffuse/density:+|-/relic/clock) to its executor — each calling EXISTING machinery only (dwalkLootSlot/dwalkValuable for hoard, rollNPC for captive, rollItem for relic, a salience pick over w.factions for faction-mark, the capOpenDispositionClock front-clock SHAPE for clock). `w` (the live world) is OPTIONAL throughout — every executor that would touch live state (faction-mark's real faction, captive's codexAdd mint, clock's w.pressures push) degrades to a walk-local placement without inventing a fact when w is absent (a lean/headless caller). Pure-lens rows (skin.grants empty) mutate nothing; unknown grant tokens log + no-op (forward-compatible). walkSkinProvenance(walk) surfaces a promise-vs-found line per placed grant (DM-held; `found` reads a caller-set `.discovered` flag, defaulting false). Table-dependent: skin.grants/skin.motif come from rollTable's row[8]/row[9], present once the three Walk Skin tables carry the Grants/Motif columns (this unit's own table pass lands them, so it's live, not dormant).

THE BREACH & THE NIGHTMARE — engine layer (docs/BREACH.md, BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2 'breach-core'/'outlandish-realms'). The walk-skin roll becomes a 2d10 bell + fray shift: rollWalkSkinBreach(envKind,{q,r,centerFn}) rolls breachShift2d10 (EXACT J2 rule: r>11 -> r+frayMod, r<11 -> r-frayMod, r==11 unchanged, clamp[2,20]; frayMod 0/+1/+2 off REGIONS-NAMES' own FRAY_1/FRAY_2), classifies the shifted result into center/nightmare/breach (NIGHTMARE_TAIL=3, BREACH_TAIL=19), and for center calls the caller's own bias-chain resolver (centerFn, defaulting to plain rollWalkSkin) BYTE-IDENTICAL to today; for a tail it rolls the compiled walk-breach-<env>/walk-nightmare-<env> table (breach-tables unit) and NULL-SAFE falls back to the center roll (tagged tailWanted) when that table isn't compiled yet — never crashes, never fabricates a row. breachPersistenceRoll(walk) — the d6 AT walk exit, once, idempotent (sealed 1-4/unstable 5/stable 6); breachStableDoor writes a write-once map-node flag for a stable outcome. breachMarkRealmActive/breachRealmWalkTaken/breachRealmClear own w.realm.debt (J2 mutation check: ONLY the original roll sets the 1d2 debt — a second call for an already-active realm is a pure no-op, never re-rolled/extended). The five physics-lens executors (breachPhysicsDcBump/ZoneStep/TechGate/HuntClock/StageVoice + the combatStart-adjacent breachApplyPhysicsToCombat wrapper) are PURE report-only functions — they compute the lens's delta and return a plain object; they never mutate HP/damage dice/AC/XP pricing and never patch any global (BREACH.md §2b's no-break invariant), leaving the actual fold-in to whichever call site (engine.check/engine.combat) chooses to read the reported delta. breachXpMultiplier(tail) is the single BREACH_XP/NIGHTMARE_XP (1.5, E(L) units) source for any future xpReport bucket. §6 (BREACH.md §2c/§2e.7, outlandish-realms unit): breachLootGuarantee(level,realms,segments) is THE ≥1-PER-BREACH GUARANTEE — rolls a flat-d4 channel (hoard/social/secret/apex), falls back social→hoard when the walk carries no Social segment (breachHasSocialSegment), then draws ONE realm-filtered Outlandish item via dwalkOutlandish(level,{inBreach:true,realms}) — inBreach:true is the ONE place reality-breaking is allowed outside the L4 gate's own level math (BREACH.md §2e.3's sourcing supersede, mirrored in src/engine/dungeon-walk.js's dwalkOutlandishAllowed). Every rollTable/frayBeyond1/frayBeyond2/mapOf/dwalkOutlandish read is typeof-guarded (BATCH-GUARDRAILS G9).

Scene Risk Contract — derives the typed fairness contract (danger/reward bands, telegraphs, escape modes, death stakes, persistent trace) stamped onto every minted walk; validator + digest projection.

The Critical-Magnitude engine (docs/CRIT-MAGNITUDE.md §1, §4) — a nat 20/1 demands a second d20 (the magnitude die). rollCritMagnitude(natural,{magnitude}) maps the band → a lens count, draws that many DISTINCT lenses from the compiled mythic-success/failure-lenses (d12), and routes the row-1 'a place is transformed/scarred' lens into the Myth suite (rolls myth-seeds). Returns an atom payload only (rolled dice + lens vectors); never writes the world — the DM narrates, then emits a crit_outcome event (world.dm) to canonize a Mythic result to the Ledger.

The Attitude/Parley/Morale RESOLVER (docs/SOCIAL.md §2-§4,§6; SOCIAL Phase 2) — the social analog of combat. PURE + DETERMINISTIC: every fn takes plain numbers/flags and returns a DELTA, never reading/writing the world. socialDC(value) = the DC to shift attitude one step friendlier (Hostile 25 → Friendly 10; Helpful terminal); applyLeverage(dc,levers) folds the NPC Want/Fear/Leverage/Trust-Lever mods (±5) and flags a decisive auto-shift; resolveSocialCheck(input) returns {outcome,from,to,shift,terrified,granted} (one check = one step; caught lie −2, miss-by-5 −1, intimidation overshoot → Terrified); moraleDC(trigger,mods)/resolveMorale(input) drive fight-or-flight (held vs. broke → caller rolls Morale Outcome); insightReadDC(input) = the scaled read-attitude DC (10 +5 guarded + best mental mod if masking). The Phase-3 event layer calls these then commits via codexSetAttitude/codexSetTerrified.

The Consequence-Ladder RESOLVER (docs/CONSEQUENCE-LADDER.md) — turns a spice-graded flavor roll into an optional, player-pulled thread without fractaling. PURE + DETERMINISTIC (mirrors engine.social): never reads/writes the world. consequenceFor({legs,band,pool}) classifies a tagged roll into a descriptor (sink + opensThread + clock + band-intensity) — consequence routes on LEGS, band sets intensity (§3/§4). clResolveEffect(pool,dieTotal) reads the pooled effect die (Hungering-Stone shape: Nature|Use|Tell|Escalation) for the PLAYER's open roll; CL_POOLS is the pluggable archetype→table registry (Watcher built; rest null → graceful degrade to DM/on-the-fly per DM-CHARTER §8.5). clBindFirst(candidates,seed) scores existing threads for reincorporation (bind-first), else null → clOnMissPlan names the roll-on-miss generator. The wiring layer (applyEvent) orchestrates latent → bind-first → roll-on-miss and commits via codex/ledger events.

The theater-of-the-mind 5.5 combat RESOLVER (docs/COMBAT.md). PURE + DETERMINISTIC (mirrors engine.social/engine.consequence): operates only on the passed transient combat objects, never on w/U/codex. THE SCRIPT OWNS THE NUMBERS — creature resolution (resolveCreature: name → BESTIARY → CR-band fallback → quick-stats), side-based initiative (rollInitiative), attack/save/damage math (resolveAttack/resolveSave/cmRollDamage; dice-bearing fns accept a pre-rolled d20 so the player's open roll drives the PC), HP/condition/range-band tracking (applyDamage/moveBand/CM_BANDS), the PC's own weapon damage (cmEquippedDamage: resolves sh.equipped + sh.inventory against data/items.js's ITEMS_BY_NAME instead of a DM-recalled o.dmg — honors the SRD base two-weapon-fighting rule, docs/ITEMS.md), and the PC's AC from worn armor (cmEquippedAC: 5.5e Light/Medium/Heavy + shield; cmSheetAC folds in the flat feat bonus sh.acBonus; defaultEquip picks a sensible starting loadout — docs/ITEMS.md). combatStart builds GS.combat (the caller stashes it); combatFromEncounter wires walk.js encounters → resolved foes (a Faction Clash segment's `enc.factions[].creatures` is a comma-joined category-member list, not a single name — split on ',' + pick one member, then resolved via engine.walk-archetypes' resolveArchetypePool same as wwalkEncounter's non-clash path; graceful fallback if that module isn't loaded); combatOutcomeEvents derives the EVENT-CONTRACT payloads (encounter_resolved + per-foe kill) which world/dm.js applyEvent emits + prices (CR-XP, objective-gated) + escalates (kill{factionId} → clock_advanced). DURABILITY-TRIO.md §2: a `rusted` instance's conditions tag (world.durability, loaded later — late-binding call) steps cmEquippedDamage's weapon die down one size (rustSteppedDie) and cmEquippedAC subtracts 1 AC per rusted armor/shield piece (cmRustAcPenalty) — both null-safe no-ops when world.durability isn't loaded. Added 2026-06-30.

Economy v1 (docs/ECONOMY.md) — the buy/sell ENGINE spine. DM-SEAT (docs/DM-SEAT.md §5.1, feat/seat-app-module) — the API-direct DM transport: message assembly (§2), validation (§3), and the settings toggle (w.dm.transport==="seat"|"mailbox", default mailbox) that lets world.dm's sendTurn branch to this module WITHOUT changing the mailbox path. seatBoot() fetches docs/SEAT-PROMPT.md once per session with a clean degrade (missing file → seat disabled, toast, seatToggleTransport refuses to switch on). seatAssembleMessages builds the §2 four-part message array (system prompt / session-bootstrap once / rolling ~12-turn window with fold-to-summary eviction / this-turn digest) with BYTE-STABLE prefix ordering across calls (no timestamps/randomness woven in) for provider prompt-caching. seatEventVocabulary() reads the explicit DM_EVENT_TYPES registry (dm.js:1218) directly — no longer a source derivation (docs/SEAT-ADAPTER.md §2); the registry is parity-locked to applyEvent's switch by dev/verify-dm-seam.mjs's RED-FIRST guard — cached after first read. seatValidate() schema-gates a parsed TurnResponse and drops unknown-typed events with a dmNotes note; seatResolveResponse() retries ONCE on a parse failure with a corrective instruction, then falls back to seatStutterEnvelope() (an in-voice stall line — the session never crashes). seatSend() is sendTurn's seat-path counterpart: assembles+POSTs to the bridge's /seat route (built by a separate unit, feat/seat-bridge-proxy — this module never holds a provider key), streams SSE narration into the feed live via seatStreamAppend (render.js's renderDMFeed reads GS.seat.streamText while GS.seat.streaming), and — per §1 "events apply then, never mid-stream" — parses/validates/applies the TurnResponse only once the stream closes, reusing world.dm's real applyResponse (one implementation of the event-apply pipeline, seat or mailbox). Tested by dev/verify-seat.mjs (jsdom, mock /seat endpoint — no key needed).

THE DURABILITY TRIO (docs/DURABILITY-TRIO.md) — three small batch-2 units bundled in one file/one verify harness (dev/verify-durability.mjs, per BATCH2-GUARDRAILS H1). §1 world export/import: exportUniverseJSON/exportWorldJSON serialize U (or one world wrapped in a minimal U) to pretty JSON; importUniverseJSON validates + merges BY WORLD ID, duplicating (never overwriting) a colliding id, running every incoming world through migrateWorld. Pure string-in/string-out — the DOM download/file-picker glue lives in genesis.html + the ⚙ Menu. §2 environmental rust: a non-magical METAL weapon/armor (rustIsMetalItem — data/items.js carries no material field, so this is a name/category heuristic reconciling the spec's trigger against what the generated data exposes, logged as an uncertainty) exposed to a qualifying hazard (rain-combat/submersion/acid — RUST_EXPOSURE_KINDS) rusts gently: first exposure sets `rusting` (a TELL, not in the generated ITEM_CONDITIONS vocab — written directly to inst.conditions rather than routed through the condition_add event's ITEM_CONDITIONS gate), a second un-maintained exposure upgrades to `rusted` (RUST_TEETH, already a parked ITEM_CONDITIONS entry per docs/ITEMS.md §D) — never worse. rustSteppedDie is the SRD weapon-die ladder step-down engine.combat's cmEquippedDamage consults for a rusted weapon; rustMaintainAll (called from passTime, any rest kind) clears every carried instance's rust. §3 Chronicle ⇐ Ledger: chronicleLine(entry) renders a ledger entry's existing `.text` as the Chronicle's HTML line (mostly passthrough + a per-type style class); chronicleMigrateLegacyLog(w) one-time-idempotently imports legacy w.log prose lines lacking a ledger twin as session-type ledger entries (stamped w._chronicleMigrated, called from migrateWorld); logEvent is redefined here as an INERT no-op shim (overriding world/state.js's w.log.unshift definition via classic-script late-declaration-wins) so its 16 existing call sites across world.play/creator.sheet/creator.levelup/world.fate/world.rebirth/engine.world-gen need no edits (every one already sits beside an equivalent addLedger call — G0 minimal-diffs). Added 2026-07-02 (durability unit, batch-2).

FOREVER STORAGE (docs/FOREVER-STORAGE.md, BATCH3-PLAN unit 13, BATCH3-GUARDRAILS J1/J2 "forever-guards") — the IndexedDB layer that keeps a many-session world off the localStorage wall. §1 saveWorld(w) persists ONLY the changed world, async, debounced (~250ms trailing, one timer per world id — saving world A never touches world B); world.state's saveU(u) is left untouched at all 37 call sites (G0 minimal-diffs) and ADDITIONALLY fires saveWorld for the active world off its synchronous localStorage write (the spec's own "keep the LS original for one release" belt-and-suspenders). migrateLStoIDB() is the boot-once import: every world in the legacy `genesis-universe-v2` blob writes into IDB, a read-back deep-equal verifies each one before the {migrated:true} stamp lands in the `meta` store — the LS blob is NEVER deleted this release, so a failed/partial migration always has the original to fall back to. storageEstimate() wraps navigator.storage.estimate() for the ⚙ Menu's storage meter (a dial, not a countdown — IDB is GB-scale). Every IDB write (storeWriteWorldNow/saveMeta/archiveAppend) is wrapped — a failure (including a real QuotaExceededError) surfaces storeHandleWriteFailure: an in-app toast + an immediate storeQuotaOffer export-download, never a silent loss; a plain no-idb ABSENCE (old browser / no shim) is explicitly NOT treated as a failure — it stays silent (saveU's synchronous localStorage write is the durable copy in that case). §2 archiveOldSessions(w) moves w.dmlog prose entries stamped with a session number <= (current session − HOT_SESSIONS, default 3) into the `archive` IDB store (one record per world id, append-only merge via archiveAppend) and strips them from the hot w.dmlog — the mechanical ledger (w.ledger) is NEVER touched here (it's small and IS the world's memory: recall/drift/reputation/chronicle all read it). archiveReadForWorld(worldId) is the Chronicle's on-demand read of what moved. The session stamp itself is a new additive field on pushDmLog's envelope (world.state — zero behavior change for existing dmlog readers, which ignore unknown keys). §3 game saves stay LOCKED ironman-always (docs/FOREVER-STORAGE.md §3) — nothing in this file adds a checkpoint/restore path; the retcon-negotiation protocol is DM-CHARTER frontier prose, explicitly out of this unit's code (BATCH-GUARDRAILS G0). storeMaybeBackupNudge() is the periodic "it's been 2 weeks — export a backup?" toast, tracked in the meta store (cosmetic scheduling, not durability-critical). NULL-SAFE throughout: no IndexedDB in the runtime (old browser, or a jsdom harness with no IDB shim) degrades every function here to a flagged {ok:false,reason:"no-idb"} — saveU's existing localStorage write is completely unaffected either way. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, forever-guards unit).

GAP-WIRING (docs/TABLE-GAPS-070126.md §7, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2) — the wiring for five wave-2a tables that shipped fully compiled (100 rows each) with no caller: chase-complications, distant-word, downtime-ledger, festival-and-holy-days, shrine-and-omen. §1 chase: chaseInit/chaseRound/chaseYield are a PURE 3-segment gap-clock (mirrors engine.combat/engine.social — operate only on the passed transient chase object; the caller owns GS.chase + ledger commits), closing on a caller-supplied pursuerWon boolean from an already-resolved opposed check, rolling one chase-complications result per round, ending in outcome:"contact"|"away". §2 distant-word: distantWordFactPool/distantWordPick salience-weight (recency-doubled, most-recent-30-days) over clock|outcome|drift ledger entries from NON-current nodes; distantWordRoll binds a Distortion row to a REAL picked fact (never invents one — degrades to fact:null rather than fabricate, the spec's named mutation check) and leaves a Color row fact-free by design; `dm.realFact` carries the true text for the DM's eyes only. §3 downtime: fixed DOWNTIME_INTENTS vocab (work/carouse/research/train/lie-low/seek-work); seek-work flags {ok:false,reason:"seek-work-unbuilt"} (routes to JOB-WALKS, not yet built — never faked, G9); the other five roll downtime-ledger once, parse payout hooks via downtimePayoutFromText (gold sign/qualifier, contact-mint/distant-word/condition/thread flags) and tier-scale gold via downtimeGoldAmount (DOWNTIME_BASE_BY_TIER, mirrors ECONOMY-SINKS' LODGING_GP tier curve). §4 festival: festivalEligibleFromDrift reports whether a drift band is Textured+ (chain-eligible, caller/DM decides); festivalRoll surfaces the roll + its own marketEffect/complication text (applying a live price multiplier is ECONOMY/SHOP-UI's job, out of scope). §5 shrine & omen: shrineOmenRoll binds every row's `` `[the myth]` `` placeholder to the world's own w.seed.myth (never invents a myth; a myth-less world leaves the placeholder, flagged not fabricated). NULL-SAFE throughout: every rollTable() call degrades to a logged no-op if a table isn't compiled (matches WORLD-TURN's convention), though all five ARE compiled today. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, gap-wiring unit).

URBAN FABRIC (docs/URBAN-FABRIC.md, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2 "urban-fabric") — typed buildings, lazy districts, the tavern as a surface. §1 rollBuilding(type,opts): the building-interior base roll + a data.building-kits TYPE KIT; shop kinds (smithy/apothecary/general/arcanist) delegate to makeShop wholesale (the kit adds the room around the counter, economy.js stays the sole stock owner); the tavern kit's namePattern ("tavern-name") consumes the Tavern-2.0-extraction compiled table. §2 district fabric (Settlement 1.1, distilled): mintDistricts(w,nodeId) mints write-once `kind:"district"` codex records linked `part-of` the node, ONCE per node (a re-entry no-ops, returning the existing ids — the J1 mutation check); districtCount(tier) is the PLACE_TIERS-keyed count (hamlet 0 · village 1 · town 1d2 · city 1d3+1); each district rolls `urban-district-type` for its character line. §3 building lifecycle: buildingApproach mints a typed building SOFT at a node — its proprietor draws from the ambient-pool path first (an already-minted soft ambient NPC at the node, per J2's "proprietors mint via the ambient-pool path"), rolling a fresh rollNPC only if none is free; buildingContact locks the building AND its proprietor to hard canon together (codexContact on both), mirroring how every other entity's soft->hard lock works. §4 the tavern's system-surfaces: tavernContactFire re-fires gap-wiring's distantWordRoll on tavern contact (no new mechanism); carouse already routes through gap-wiring's generic downtimeIntent (a tavern is simply WHERE that intent gets declared, not a second venue gate); the proprietor being minted `at` the node satisfies prep.js's nodeOwnerAttitude for free (the lodging-owner tint). WIRING-SWEEP-A §6 (docs/WIRING-MAP.md item 5, world.wiring-a): buildingContact's tavern branch also rolls tavernEncounterRoll — a chance-gated (0.35) tavern-encounters ambient beat. NULL-SAFE throughout (matches WORLD-TURN's convention): an unknown type, missing kit data, or an uncompiled table all degrade to a flagged {ok:false,reason} or a null sub-field, never a fabricated result. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, urban-fabric unit).

JOB WALKS (docs/JOB-WALKS.md, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J1/J2 "job-walks") — the 300-row npc-job-board SCALES (pay + threat by place tier) and accepting a posting MINTS a real 1-3 segment walk (Adam's directive: "infinite quests!"). §1 jobPosting/jobBoardRead: one/2-3 tier-scaled postings per board read — tier from nodeLodgingTier + region econTilt (the same signals ECONOMY-SINKS/open_shop already reuse, no new heuristic), pay = TIER_PAY[tier] mildly tier-compounded, envHint a uniform urban/wilderness/dungeon roll (the row text carries no env tag — a guessed text-match would violate G9, so this is a fresh roll), poster a rolled NPC minted soft into the codex. §2 jobWalkAccept: segments = 1+tier via jobWalkSegCount, threat=tier, routed to rollUrbanWalk (urban, stays at the current node) or rollWildernessWalk/rollDungeonWalk (wilderness/dungeon — OFF-city per §3, mints a fresh destination node + rolls a route exactly like play.js's explore()); stores under prep.js's P.nodes keyed by the (possibly-new) destination node with kind:"job", activates via walkSetActive — a REAL walk with real provenance, nothing bespoke. jobWalkPayout (called from prep.js's walkComplete kind:"job" branch): pays gold directly onto the living sheet, warms the poster's attitude + locks them to a real contact on completion (recurring employers), flags followUp. §3 jobBoardTick (wired into worldTurn's montage branch, src/world/turn.js): the TTL sweep (4+1d4 days) that resolves an unclaimed posting WITHOUT the player — 1d6: 1-3 someone-else-took-it (ledger line only), 4-6 it-got-worse (bumps the poster's linked faction clock +1 IF repuFactionOf resolves one; a bare rolled NPC carries no faction link in this codebase today, so that half degrades to a flagged no-op rather than inventing an attribution — this is the mutation check the spec names: "persist forever" fails once this sweep exists and is called). gap-wiring.js's downtimeIntent seek-work branch now calls jobBoardRead directly (closing that unit's flagged no-op). NULL-SAFE throughout: an uncompiled npc-job-board, a missing walk roller, or an unknown posting id all degrade to a flagged {ok:false,reason}, never a fabricated result. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, job-walks unit).

WIRING-SWEEP-A (docs/WIRING-MAP.md §B Wave A, docs/BATCH3-PLAN.md unit 10, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J1 "wiring-sweep-A") — the Wave-A wire-in queue minus npc-job-board (promoted to its own unit, job-walks.js): the remaining seven true orphans. §1 REST-RISK: restRiskRoll grades a rest's SECURITY CLASS (inn/camp/wild/dungeon, derived from nodeLodgingTier+nodeInhabited+the walk env — the only real per-node signals this codebase carries) and rolls the matching urban-/dungeon-rest-complications table; a row whose OWN TEXT reads as a violent interruption can INTERRUPT the rest (restRiskSevere — never a guessed Spice band, neither table carries one). Wired into play.js's passTime. §2 IF-IGNORED: turnIgnoredCheck sweeps codex thread records (dm.legs hook/thread-seed, unresolved) stale past IGNORED_STALE_DAYS, rolls npc-if-ignored (+regional-effects when region-tagged), ledgers a drift entry, and resets the staleness window — wired into worldTurn's montage branch (src/world/turn.js), same shape as repuFadeTick/jobBoardTick. §3 parleyWantRoll: creature-parley-wants rolled by monster-tactics' morale seam (src/world/dm.js foe_morale) the instant a foe breaks to "surrender" — stashed as foe.parleyWant, SOCIAL's parley_open defaults p.want from it when the caller doesn't supply one. §4 huntedBehaviorRoll: monster-behavior-if-hunted rolled the instant a foe breaks to "flee"/"rout-panic" — stashed as foe.huntedBehavior (feeds a future chase_start caller; that caller is gap-wiring's own flagged-open follow-up, out of this unit's scope — see file header). §5 regionEncounterRoll: region-encounter as an additive per-leg regional-flavor roll, gated on a region actually being present (null region ⇒ null, byte-identical fallback). The "malformed header" flag did NOT reproduce against current source/compiled reality (hand-verified before writing this file, G9) — no repair needed. §6 tavernEncounterRoll: tavern-encounters as a chance-gated (0.35) ambient beat alongside urban.js's buildingContact tavern branch. §7 walkPickInteractable: urban-interactable-object/wilderness-interactable-object — the same segment-object slot dungeon-walk.js already wires for dungeons, called from src/engine/walk.js (urban) and src/engine/wild-walk.js (wilderness) per non-finale segment/leg. §8 seed dispatch (urban-rumor-intel/urban-catalyst + the ≥1-non-urban-seed rider): VERIFIED already wired (rollUrbanWalk's existing Rumor branch + setup.catalyst/finale catalystCallback) and already structurally guaranteed (engine.prep-bundle's pbundlePlan always assembles one each of urban/dungeon/wilderness) — no code change needed, harness verifies the property directly.
